headlines.title: 4 High-Yield Dividend Stocks for Retirees Who Want Income They Can Count On
headlines.summary: Yields above 8% tempt retirees, but the real question is whether the cash behind each check is strong enough to cover it. Four companies tied to tolls, rent, and phone bills face that test, and one carries a tax wrinkle many IRA owners miss.

headlines.title: Verizon Pays Out $11.7 Billion a Year in Dividends. Here’s the Free Cash Flow Math Behind Its 6.2%-Yielding Payout.
headlines.summary: Verizon is a cash flow machine.

headlines.title: Musk Says AT&T and Verizon May “Lose Some Revenue” as Starlink’s Phone Service Gets 40x the Bandwidth
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysElon Musk said SpaceX’s next direct-to-cell satellites, launching in 2027, will have 40x the bandwidth, and AT&T and Verizon may lose some revenue. The hit looks small for now, since satellite signals struggle to reach phones indoors, but SpaceX’s planned rooftop micro cell towers aim at that gap.

headlines.title: How Retirees Can Turn $450,000 Into Passive Income With These 5 Dividend Stocks
headlines.summary: Selling shares in a downturn can turn a temporary loss into a permanent one for retirees. Five dividend payers from five sectors might offer a way out, but each hides a risk worth knowing before you commit a dollar.

headlines.title: How AI Contracts Will Impact Verizon (VZ) Investors
headlines.summary: Verizon Communications has secured close to US$4b in long-term AI infrastructure contracts and deepened its IoT reach through deals such as Bosch Motorsport’s global race-day deployment on Verizon’s Global IoT Orchestration and ThingSpace platforms. The Bosch Motorsport rollout highlights how Verizon can apply its IoT stack to mission-critical, high-density environments. This showcases potential demand for managed connectivity and telemetry services beyond its core consumer wireless base.

description: Verizon Communications Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the provision of communications, technology, information, and streaming products and services to consumers, businesses, and governmental entities worldwide. It operates in two segments, Verizon Consumer Group (Consumer) and Verizon Business Group (Business). The Consumer segment provides wireless services across the wireless networks in the United States under the Verizon and TracFone brands and through wholesale and other arrangements; and fixed wireless access (FWA) broadband through its wireless networks, as well as related equipment and devices, such as smartphones, tablets, smartwatches, and other wireless-enabled connected devices. The segment also offers wireline services in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeastern United States, as well as Washington D.C. through its fiber-optic network, Verizon Fios product portfolio, and a copper-based network. The Business segment provides wireless and wireline communications services and products, including FWA and wireline broadband, advanced communication services, corporate networking, security and managed network, local and long-distance voice, and network access services to deliver various IoT services and products to businesses, government customers, and wireless and wireline carriers in the United States and internationally. The company distributes its products and services through direct channels, company-operated stores, digital and omnichannel platforms, indirect agents, business solution resellers, and national retailers. The company was formerly known as Bell Atlantic Corporation and changed its name to Verizon Communications Inc. in June 2000. Verizon Communications Inc. was incorporated in 1983 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
